feature: Customer Portal v2 -- the Risk Register (/portal-v2/risk-register), WIRED TO REAL DATA. The page previously rendered the design fixture RR_RISKS (twelve fictional Halden Materials risks); it now renders the calling customer's own rows from msp_risk_decisions via GET /api/portal/risk-register, scoped by (msp_id, tenants.tenantId) off the JWT. This manifest covers the real read, the real acceptance write path's guards, and the DOM integration between them.
notes: WHAT CHANGED AND WHY THE OLD ASSERTIONS ARE GONE. The previous version of this manifest was 58 steps asserting the FIXTURE: '12 risks shown', '19 pts', '34 pts', '3 open + 2 mitigating', and risk ids RSK-001..RSK-012. Those were correct against a page reading RR_RISKS at module scope. The page now reads the customer's real register, so every one of those numbers is now false for any real tenant and asserting them would guarantee a red run. They are replaced, not deleted quietly -- the derivations they used to pin (filter predicates, the reproduced prototype defects, the stable-sort behaviour) are still pinned, in src/components/portal-v2/riskRegisterModel.test.ts and riskRegisterWire.test.ts, which run over the fixture on purpose.

THE NUMBERS BELOW COME FROM SEEDED ROWS, AND THAT IS STATED PLAINLY. The testbed tenant had NO risk decisions -- the table's only row belonged to 'contoso-01', a synthetic tenant identifier matching no real tenant -- so both pages rendered empty. lib/db/migrations/manual/2026-08-21-portal-v2-risk-register-testbed-seed.sql seeds four rows against msp_id 1 + tenant c4c814d4-3afe-441e-9145-62461d0a4fd3 (tenants.id 1, the tenant behind TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL). The READ PATH, the SCOPING and the WRITE PATH are real; the row CONTENT is seeded demonstration data. Re-run that seed if these assertions drift.

EXPECTED REGISTER (from the seed): RBD-2026-101 Security/Mitigating weight 9, RBD-2026-102 Compliance/Accepted weight 6 (already signed by Priya Raman), RBD-2026-103 Governance/Open weight 4, RBD-2026-104 Compliance/Accepted weight 3 (signed by Rowan Clarke). Totals therefore: 4 on the register, 1 open + 1 mitigating, 2 accepted decisions, 9 pts suppressed (6+3), 13 pts still counting (9+4). Default sort is heaviest-first, so RBD-2026-101 is row 0 and opens expanded.

THE ACCEPTANCES-NEEDING-ATTENTION BAND IS ABSENT ON PURPOSE. It renders only when a risk is Expired or its acceptance runs out in the current year; both seeded acceptances run to 2027, so `expiring.length` is 0 and the band is not rendered at all. RR14 asserts that absence rather than leaving it unstated.

WHY NO HAPPY-PATH ACCEPT IS DRIVEN HERE, AND WHAT COVERS IT INSTEAD. An acceptance is PERMANENT by design -- the route refuses a second one with 409 -- so a manifest step that successfully accepted a risk would pass exactly once and be red on every subsequent run. This manifest therefore drives the three guards that ARE idempotent (400 with the checkbox missing, 409 on an already-accepted risk, 404 on another tenant's id), and the successful write is pinned by src/routes/portal-risk-register.test.ts, which asserts the typed name is stored and that acceptedAt / ipAddress / signatureHash are derived server-side and NOT taken from the request body. A5 is the one that matters most: it proves the permanence guarantee end-to-end against the real database.

THE LOGIN BLOCK IS NOT OPTIONAL. /portal-v2/* sits behind ProtectedRoute; a probe that skips the login steps hits the login screen and every assertion fails for an unrelated reason. On a WebView2 that is already authenticated, the two `input` steps (#email/#password) fail while the rest runs green -- that is a known harness artefact, not a page fault.
UI ROUTE SHAPE: msp-portal's outer WouterRouter has base '/portal' and SlugScope nests a second router at '/{slug}', so the real URL is /portal/{slug}/portal-v2/risk-register.

ROLE FLOOR IS CustomerUser, DELIBERATELY HIGHER than the Assessment floor used by portal-change-control / portal-remediation-tracker -- the register carries dollar liability exposure and a signature surface. TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL (shanemccaw+buyassessment@outlook.com) is a real CustomerUser, verified against the users/tenants join, so the harness reaches it.
shaneapp://runTest hits the DEPLOYED build, not the local worktree.
ENV VARS required in BuildConsole -> Settings -> Test Environment Variables: DEPLOY_URL, TEST_PORTAL_EMAIL / TEST_PORTAL_PASSWORD, TEST_PORTAL_SLUG.

apiTests.name: SETUP -- log in as the designated TESTBED account; extract the bearer.
A1 -- the customer-scoped register answers, and answers with an ARRAY. This is the endpoint that did not exist before this build; msp-rbd.ts served the same table MSPOperator-only.
A2 -- extract the FIRST risk's id. The route orders by id DESC, so this is RBD-2026-104. UI6 asserts this exact id reaches the DOM, which is the real API-to-DOM integration proof.
A3 -- extract a real title off the wire, for the same reason.
A4 -- THE CHECKBOX IS MANDATORY. `confirmed` is z.literal(true), so an acceptance without the customer ticking the box is malformed rather than merely 'not accepted'.

body.statement: I understand and accept this risk.

apiTests.name: A5 -- AN ACCEPTANCE IS PERMANENT. RBD-2026-102 was signed on 12 August 2026; a second acceptance, with a different name, is refused 409 against the real database. This is the whole promise of the flow -- timestamped, permanent, never editable after the fact -- proven end-to-end rather than only in a mocked unit test.

body.statement: I understand and accept this risk.

apiTests.name: A6 -- a risk id outside the caller's own tenant answers 404, NOT 403, so the endpoint cannot be used to enumerate which RBD ids exist. RBD-2026-575 is real, but belongs to the 'contoso-01' tenant.

body.statement: I understand and accept this risk.

apiTests.name: A7 -- a typed name of one character is refused: the signature has to be a name, not a keystroke.

body.statement: I understand and accept this risk.

apiTests.name: A8 -- the Policy Decisions view of the same table answers with an array.

uiSteps.name: goto the real login URL (outer WouterRouter base = '/portal').
WAIT for the login form to hydrate before typing.
Primary login -- every assertion below needs a real session.
goto the Risk Register on its slug-scoped route.
UI1 -- the page resolved to the register, not NotFound and not the param pillar route.
UI2 -- THE LIVE READ SUCCEEDED. The status line renders only while loading or on error, so its absence is the proof the fetch resolved rather than silently failing to an empty register.
UI3 -- four risks on the real register, not the fixture's twelve.
UI4 -- stat card 1 counts the customer's own register.
UI5 -- ...and its sub-line breaks those four down by their REAL statuses.
UI6 -- API-TO-DOM: the id the API returned at $.risks[0].id is rendered on the page. Interpolated from A2, so this cannot pass against a hardcoded string.
UI7 -- API-TO-DOM: so is the title the API returned. Interpolated from A3.
UI8 -- 9 points suppressed: the two accepted risks' weights (6+3), computed over live rows.
UI9 -- 13 points still counting: the Mitigating 9 plus the Open 4.
UI10 -- the explainer restates the suppressed total with the other suffix, mid-sentence, from the same live figure.
UI11 -- default sort is heaviest-first, so the weight-9 risk is row 0 and opens expanded.
UI12 -- the expanded body carries the real hazard description off the database row, not a summary.
uiSteps.textContains: IMAP and SMTP AUTH are reachable

uiSteps.name: UI13 -- and the compensating controls stored as jsonb are rendered as the row's controls.
UI14 -- the acceptances-needing-attention band is ABSENT: both seeded acceptances run to 2027, so nothing qualifies. Asserted rather than left unstated.
UI15 -- open the already-accepted risk.
UI16 -- ONE ROW OPEN AT A TIME: opening it closed row 0.
UI17 -- THE REAL ACCEPTANCE IS ON SCREEN: the register entry it was filed under, straight off register_ref.
UI18 -- ...the name that was TYPED to accept it, out of client_approver.name.

UI19 -- ...and the acceptance date, formatted from the accepted_at timestamp IN UTC. A local-timezone format would render this as 11 August for anyone west of Greenwich; on a permanent liability record the date must not move with the reader.
UI20 -- ...and its stored rationale, verbatim from the database.
UI21 -- an already-accepted risk offers no second decision, so the three-card action grid is absent. The UI refuses what the route would 409.
UI22 -- DEEP LINK, over live rows: ?pillar=Governance filters to the one Governance risk.
UI23 -- one risk shown.
UI24 -- and it is the Governance one.
UI25 -- the Security risk is filtered out.
UI26 -- the stat cards do NOT move with the filter; they are computed over the whole register.
UI27 -- ?pillar=Compliance catches the two Compliance rows.
UI28 -- two risks shown.
UI29 -- an unrecognised pillar is ignored rather than filtering everything away.
UI30 -- ...so the register is whole again.
UI31 -- INERT BY DESIGN, still rendered rather than trimmed: the header's Export register.
